note: First cut of the corpus. Works are economic entities, not tech-tree nodes — see docs/05-knowledge-economy.md. Ancient dating is conventional and confidence-tagged; NOT yet reviewed by a specialist, and several entries touch texts sacred to living communities.

pillars.name: Design
pillars.arc: Craft and form. Pottery and bead-drilling → bronze → temple sculpture → textile design → industrial design.

pillars.name: Information
pillars.arc: The technology of storing and moving knowledge. Mnemonic recitation → Brahmi → palm leaf → paper → print → digital. The oldest pillar and the one that never stops mattering.

pillars.name: Structure
pillars.arc: Building and engineering. Tanks and step-wells → stupas → temples → forts → canals → rail.

pillars.name: Classicism
pillars.arc: Codification: turning practice into shastra. Grammar, poetics, law, mathematics, medicine, music — the disciplines themselves.

pillars.name: Networking
pillars.arc: Connective tissue. Guru-shishya lineages, monastic circuits, merchant guilds (shreni), pilgrimage routes, later post and telegraph.

pillars.name: Trade
pillars.arc: Exchange. Barter → grain-standard → punch-marked coin → cash economy → markets.

pillars.name: Cultivation
pillars.arc: Cultivation of people: schooling, apprenticeship, ordination, discipline. Distinct from agriculture — this grows minds, not grain.

pillars.name: Agriculture
pillars.arc: Food. Foraging → domestication → irrigation → double-cropping → the plantation and the mill.

catastrophes.name: Palm-leaf decay
catastrophes.note: Not an event — a permanent condition. Palm leaf survives roughly 300 years in Indian humidity. Every work must be recopied within that window or it is gone. This is the corpus's standing upkeep cost and the single most important mechanic in the game.

catastrophes.name: Alchon Huna disruption of the north-west
catastrophes.note: Monastic and urban destruction in Gandhara and the Punjab; Taxila does not recover.

catastrophes.name: Arab conquest of Sindh
catastrophes.note: Conquest and reorganisation; scholarly exchange follows as well as loss.

catastrophes.name: Ghaznavid raids
catastrophes.note: Repeated raids including Somnath. Al-Biruni travels in their wake and writes the finest ethnography of India by an outsider — the same era produces both.

catastrophes.name: Sack of Nalanda
catastrophes.note: Bakhtiyar Khalji. The largest single loss in the corpus's history; the library reportedly burned for months. Much Indian Buddhist scholarship survives today only in Tibetan and Chinese translation — which is exactly the redundancy mechanic, working.

catastrophes.name: Timur's sack of Delhi
catastrophes.note: Massive urban destruction; scholars deported to Samarkand — loss to India, transmission elsewhere.

catastrophes.name: Portuguese suppression in Goa and the Malabar
catastrophes.note: The Goa Inquisition; destruction of Konkani and Hindu texts. Well documented, and comparatively little studied.

catastrophes.name: Colonial manuscript removal
catastrophes.note: Not burning — taking. Tens of thousands of Indian manuscripts enter European collections. The books are not destroyed; they are elsewhere. This turns the late game from rescue into repatriation.

catastrophes.name: Partition
catastrophes.note: Libraries and personal collections split, abandoned, burned in the violence.

works.title: Village story cycles
works.subject: story
works.note: Procedurally generated per region. No text survives; the mechanic does. This is where the game begins and where the storyteller is first paid in grain.

works.title: Bhimbetka rock painting tradition
works.subject: record
works.note: The oldest surviving information technology in the subcontinent.

works.title: Rigveda
works.subject: hymn
works.note: Transmitted orally with extraordinary fidelity for ~3,000 years before being written. The mnemonic schemes (padapatha, kramapatha, ghanapatha) are error-correcting codes — the finest pre-modern information technology anywhere.

works.title: Samaveda
works.subject: music
works.note: The root of Indian music theory.

works.title: Yajurveda
works.subject: ritual
works.note: Ritual procedure — and with it, altar geometry.

works.title: Atharvaveda
works.subject: medicine
works.note: Healing, herbs, household life. The most everyday of the four.

works.title: Shatapatha Brahmana
works.subject: ritual
works.note: Contains altar-construction geometry — applied mathematics in a ritual manual.

works.title: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad
works.subject: philosophy
works.note: Among the oldest Upanishads; philosophy as dialogue.

works.title: Katha Upanishad
works.subject: philosophy
works.note: Nachiketa and Death — a story that carries a philosophy. The storytelling economy at full power.

works.title: Shulba Sutras
works.subject: mathematics
works.note: Geometry for building altars, including a statement of the Pythagorean relation.

works.title: Ashtadhyayi
works.subject: grammar
works.note: 3,959 rules generating a natural language, with metarules, a formal notation and ordered rule application. Roughly 2,400 years before Backus–Naur form. The single most important artefact in this corpus.

works.title: Nirukta
works.subject: lexicon
works.note: Etymology; predates Panini.

works.title: Chandahshastra
works.subject: poetics
works.note: Prosody — and in enumerating metres, binary numeration, the Fibonacci sequence and a form of Pascal's triangle.

works.title: Mahabhashya
works.subject: grammar
works.note: The commentary that made Panini teachable. Commentary as an economic act.

works.title: Mahabharata
works.subject: epic
works.note: ~100,000 verses, grown over eight centuries. The largest single employer of storytellers in the game.

works.title: Ramayana
works.subject: epic
works.note: Retold in every language and half of Asia. The clearest case of a work whose value multiplies with derivation.

works.title: Bhagavad Gita
works.subject: philosophy
works.note: A work embedded inside a work — and eventually more copied than its host.

works.title: Panchatantra
works.subject: story
works.note: Travels to Pahlavi, then Arabic as Kalila wa Dimna, then Hebrew, Latin and every European language. The Sanskrit original is lost; the world kept the copies. Redundancy, proven.

works.title: Brihatkatha
works.subject: story
works.note: **Completely lost.** Survives only through three later Sanskrit adaptations. The canonical teaching case: a work can vanish while its children live.

works.title: Kathasaritsagara
works.subject: story
works.note: 21,000 verses reconstructing a lost ocean of stories for a Kashmiri queen.

works.title: Vetala Panchavimshati
works.subject: story
works.note: Twenty-five riddle-tales; a corpse that will not stop telling stories until you answer.

works.title: Jataka tales
works.subject: story
works.note: 547 previous-life stories; carved on stupa railings, so the story becomes architecture.

works.title: Sukasaptati
works.subject: story
works.note: Seventy tales of a parrot; later reworked in Persian as the Tutinama.

works.title: Pali Canon (Tipitaka)
works.subject: philosophy
works.note: Oral for four centuries, first written in Sri Lanka c. 29 BCE — a deliberate act of redundancy against famine and war.

works.title: Milindapanha
works.subject: philosophy
works.note: A Greek king and a Buddhist monk argue. Cross-cultural transmission as literature.

works.title: Abhidharmakosha
works.subject: philosophy
works.note: Sanskrit original lost for centuries; recovered in Tibet in 1935. Redundancy across borders, recovered after 700 years.

works.title: Pramanavarttika
works.subject: philosophy
works.note: Logic and epistemology at Nalanda. Much survives only in Tibetan.

works.title: Tattvartha Sutra
works.subject: philosophy
works.note: Accepted by every Jain sect — a rare unifying text.

works.title: Jain Agamas
works.subject: philosophy
works.note: Svetambara canon; the Digambaras hold the original was lost — a schism about redundancy itself.

works.title: Arthashastra
works.subject: statecraft
works.note: Lost for centuries; a palm-leaf manuscript surfaced in Mysore in 1905. Taxation, espionage, mining, irrigation — and the mandala theory of graded sovereignty this game is built on.

works.title: Manusmriti
works.subject: law
works.note: Enormously influential and enormously contested; Ambedkar burned a copy in 1927. The game models its influence, not its authority.

works.title: Natyashastra
works.subject: drama
works.note: Theatre, dance, music, stagecraft and rasa theory in one treatise. The design pillar's foundation document.

works.title: Charaka Samhita
works.subject: medicine
works.note: Internal medicine; translated into Arabic and thence to Europe.

works.title: Sushruta Samhita
works.subject: medicine
works.note: Surgery: 300 procedures, 120 instruments, and rhinoplasty. Reached Britain in 1794 and changed European plastic surgery.

works.title: Ashtanga Hridayam
works.subject: medicine
works.note: The synthesis that made the two older systems teachable.

works.title: Kamasutra
works.subject: philosophy
works.note: More a manual of urbane living than its reputation suggests — the sixty-four arts are a curriculum.

works.title: Krishi-Parashara
works.subject: agronomy
works.note: Ploughing, monsoon prediction, cattle, seed. The agriculture pillar in text form.

works.title: Vrikshayurveda
works.subject: agronomy
works.note: Plant science: propagation, soil, disease. A single manuscript in the Bodleian preserved it.

works.title: Samarangana Sutradhara
works.subject: architecture
works.note: Architecture, town planning and mechanical devices, by a king who wrote his own treatises.

works.title: Mayamata
works.subject: architecture
works.note: South Indian temple architecture and iconometry.

works.title: Sangita Ratnakara
works.subject: music
works.note: The bridge text: both Hindustani and Carnatic traditions claim it.

works.title: Rasaratnakara
works.subject: metallurgy
works.note: Alchemy and metallurgy; zinc distillation at Zawar predates Europe by centuries.

works.title: Bakhshali manuscript
works.subject: mathematics
works.note: Contains a dot for zero. Radiocarbon dating is disputed — a live scholarly argument the game should present as one.

works.title: Aryabhatiya
works.subject: astronomy
works.note: 121 verses: place-value, a sine table, π to four places, and the earth rotating on its axis.

works.title: Brahmasphutasiddhanta
works.subject: mathematics
works.note: **The first text anywhere to treat zero as a number and give rules for negatives.** Carried to Baghdad in 771 and thence to Europe. The highest-value single export in the corpus.

works.title: Ganita Sara Sangraha
works.subject: mathematics
works.note: The first Indian text purely on mathematics, without astronomy attached.

works.title: Lilavati
works.subject: mathematics
works.note: Arithmetic taught through puzzles addressed to a girl. Pedagogy as literature — a textbook that is also a story.

works.title: Siddhanta Shiromani
works.subject: astronomy
works.note: Contains an early statement of the derivative and of instantaneous motion.

works.title: Tantrasangraha
works.subject: astronomy
works.note: Kerala school; a partially heliocentric planetary model.

works.title: Yuktibhasha
works.subject: mathematics
works.note: **Infinite series for π, sine and cosine — with proofs — roughly 200 years before Newton and Leibniz.** Written in Malayalam, not Sanskrit, and largely unknown outside Kerala until the 1830s. The corpus's greatest failure of networking.

works.title: Tolkappiyam
works.subject: grammar
works.note: Grammar and poetics; the oldest surviving Tamil work.

works.title: Sangam anthologies
works.subject: poetry
works.note: 2,381 poems by 473 named poets, including many women. Nearly lost; recovered from palm leaf in the 1880s by U. V. Swaminatha Iyer — a one-man rescue that is itself a playable scenario.

works.title: Tirukkural
works.subject: philosophy
works.note: 1,330 couplets on ethics, governance and love, claimed by every Tamil tradition at once.

works.title: Silappatikaram
works.subject: epic
works.note: A merchant's wife burns a city down. The great Tamil epic and a portrait of Indian Ocean trade.

works.title: Manimekalai
works.subject: epic
works.note: Its sequel, and Buddhist.

works.title: Tevaram
works.subject: poetry
works.note: Bhakti hymns sung on pilgrimage routes — knowledge distributed by walking.

works.title: Nalayira Divya Prabandham
works.subject: poetry
works.note: Includes Andal, one of the great women poets of any tradition.

works.title: Kamba Ramayanam
works.subject: epic
works.note: Not a translation — a rival. Derivation as creation.

works.title: Abhijnanashakuntalam
works.subject: drama
works.note: Translated by William Jones in 1789; Goethe wrote a poem about it. India's first global literary export of the modern era.

works.title: Meghaduta
works.subject: poetry
works.note: A cloud carries a message across the whole subcontinent — a geography lesson disguised as a love poem.

works.title: Mrichchhakatika
works.subject: drama
works.note: A merchant, a courtesan and a coup. Unusually secular and unusually funny.

works.title: Harshacharita
works.subject: history
works.note: A court biography — the first sustained Indian attempt at one.

works.title: Kadambari
works.subject: story
works.note: Arguably the first novel in any language; left unfinished and completed by his son.

works.title: Kavyadarsha
works.subject: poetics
works.note: Travelled to Tibet, Sri Lanka and Java — Indian literary theory as an export good.

works.title: Rajatarangini
works.subject: history
works.note: The first Indian work that is recognisably history: sources weighed, chronology argued, kings criticised.

works.title: Gita Govinda
works.subject: poetry
works.note: Set to music everywhere it went; the most illustrated Indian text after the epics.

works.title: Tarikh al-Hind
works.subject: history
works.note: Al-Biruni learned Sanskrit to write it, and wrote it in the same decades as the Ghaznavid raids. **The corpus records destruction and transmission happening simultaneously, because they did.**

works.title: Amir Khusrau's divans
works.subject: poetry
works.note: Qawwali, the sitar's ancestry, and early Hindavi verse. Synthesis as a creative act.

works.title: Baburnama
works.subject: history
works.note: A conqueror's memoir that spends more pages on melons and gardens than on battles.

works.title: Ain-i-Akbari
works.subject: statecraft
works.note: **The richest pre-colonial dataset that exists for the region:** subah, sarkar and pargana with assessed revenue and measured area. The anchor pour for the entire Mughal era.

works.title: Sirr-i-Akbar
works.subject: philosophy
works.note: Fifty Upanishads into Persian. Reaching Europe via Latin in 1801, it gave Schopenhauer the Upanishads. **Transmission through the era the game will be tempted to render only as loss.**

works.title: Bhagavata Purana
works.subject: story
works.note: The engine of the bhakti movement and of a thousand painting cycles.

works.title: Vachanas of the Sharanas
works.subject: poetry
works.note: Free verse by weavers, potters and washerwomen alongside ministers. A deliberate assault on who is allowed to produce knowledge.

works.title: Kabir's dohas
works.subject: poetry
works.note: A weaver, transmitted orally, claimed by Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs alike.

works.title: Ramcharitmanas
works.subject: epic
works.note: The Ramayana in a spoken language. Recited publicly to this day — the storytelling economy still running.

works.title: Guru Granth Sahib
works.subject: poetry
works.attributed_to: Sikh Gurus, and Hindu and Muslim saints
works.note: Compiled deliberately as a canon, including poets from outside the tradition — an act of curation as much as composition.

works.title: Abhangas of Tukaram
works.subject: poetry
works.note: Tradition holds his manuscripts were thrown into the Indrayani river and resurfaced. A story about the survival of texts, told by the text.

works.title: Hind Swaraj
works.subject: statecraft
works.note: Written in ten days on a ship; banned by the Raj on publication.

works.title: Gitanjali
works.subject: poetry
works.note: Nobel Prize, 1913 — the first for anyone outside Europe.

works.title: Anandamath
works.subject: epic
works.note: Contains Vande Mataram; also a contested text in modern politics, which the game should say rather than hide.

works.title: Annihilation of Caste
works.subject: philosophy
works.note: An undelivered speech, self-published after the invitation was withdrawn. The most direct challenge in the corpus to the corpus itself.

works.title: The Discovery of India
works.subject: history
works.note: Written in Ahmednagar Fort prison.

works.title: Constitution of India
works.subject: law
works.note: The longest written constitution of any sovereign country, and the last work in the campaign. Handwritten and illuminated — a manuscript, deliberately.
